# Draft:This Time It's War

'''This Time It's War' was an American metal band from Richmond, Virginia. Active from 2004 to 2012, the band released The Faded Grey EP in 2005, two demos in 2006 and 2008, the full-length Terror Plots in 2010, and the split EP Rusted Screws & Machinery of Man'' with Fixtures in 2011, before disbanding in 2012 and reuniting for a final show in 2016.
History
Formation and early years (2004–2008)
The band was formed in 2004 by drummer John Gammon, guitarists Alan Simpson and Justin Lawson, and bassist Vincent Riquier, who met one another in high school. The band's earliest recorded output was The Faded Grey EP in 2005, with Blake Bryant on vocals. In January 2006, the band took part in the first Virginia Metal & Hardcore Festival in Fredericksburg, Virginia, appearing on a bill that included On Broken Wings, From a Second Story Window, Through the Eyes of the Dead, Despised Icon, and Ed Gein.
In summer 2006, Bryant was replaced by vocalist Reeves Hankins, who departed in August 2006 without appearing on any recordings. Later that year, the band issued a demo with Bobby Hazelwood on vocals.
In January 2007, the band undertook an East Coast tour that included dates in Maryland, Pennsylvania, New York, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Florida, Alabama, and Virginia. In November 2007, Lambgoat reported that Scott Quigley, formerly of The Kidnapping, had joined the band as vocalist (replacing Hazelwood) and that Riquier had departed amicably.
By 2008, Jeff Jennings had joined on bass, and the lineup of Gammon, Simpson, Lawson, Quigley, and Jennings, which remained intact for the remainder of the band's career, recorded a second demo. In the fall of 2008, the band toured with Periphery on a run of Midwestern and East Coast dates. That November, the band opened for Lamb of God at the National in Richmond, a sold-out show the members later described as the most memorable of their career.
Terror Plots and later activity (2009–2012)
Terror Plots, the band's first and only full-length album, was recorded in 2009 and released on November 12, 2010. It was produced and mixed by Chris Dowhan at Planet Red Studio. The album has been described as a blend of material written during the band's early years with songs composed closer to the time of recording. In a 2010 review, Aversionline wrote that the album showed considerable growth from the band's earlier work and described the material as moving toward a more technical sound with progressive metal elements. In a 2011 interview, Simpson said the recording process stretched over roughly six months for ten songs before the album's eventual late-2010 release. Guitar Messenger described the album as fusing elements of progressive and modern metal with a political sensibility more commonly associated with the hardcore scene. In December 2010, the band appeared on the Darkest Hour Legacy Tour, opening for Darkest Hour, Periphery, and Veil of Maya at a Richmond date.
In 2011, the band released Rusted Screws & Machinery Of Man, a split EP with fellow Richmond band Fixtures.
The band remained active through 2012 before disbanding, and later reunited for a final show in 2016.
Musical style and reception
A 2007 Aversionline review of the band's 2006 demo described its sound as rooted in melodic Swedish death metal, while also noting dual-guitar harmonies, technical flourishes, and prominent solos. RVA Mag described the band as among the more technically accomplished and distinctive metal groups to emerge from Richmond, noting that online reviewers differed in how to categorize their sound, with comparisons drawn to Darkest Hour and Opeth. Aversionline's review of Terror Plots characterized the album as more technical than the earlier demo and noted progressive metal elements, while comparing aspects of its approach to Misery Signals, Darkest Hour, and Meshuggah. A December 2011 review of Rusted Screws & Machinery Of Man in RVA Mag characterized the band's contribution as melodic-leaning metalcore with a tendency that made their songs stand out from the genre. Guitar Messenger similarly noted the album's blend of progressive and modern metal elements.
Members
Final lineup
* John Gammon – drums (2004–2012, 2016)
* Justin Lawson – guitar (2004–2012, 2016)
* Alan Simpson – guitar (2004–2012, 2016)
* Jeff Jennings – bass, keyboards (2007–2012, 2016)
* Scott Quigley – vocals (2007–2012, 2016)
Former members
* Vincent Riquier – bass (2004–2007); later a founding bassist of Bad Omens
* Blake Bryant – vocals (2004–2006)
* Reeves Hankins – vocals (2006)
* Bobby Hazelwood – vocals (2006–2007)
